% Regenerate rather than hand-edit.
%
% Subtypes are DERIVED, not read off a donor: H from the segment-4 (HA) donor,
% N from the segment-6 (NA) donor. Because the two segments come from different
% strains, a chimera's subtype generally matches neither donor's own subtype
% (e.g. Set 1 Dataset-1 is H11N8; its HA donor is H11N9, its NA donor H3N8).

2		& Yes			& Mixture	& Dataset-1 (H5N1, H5N8, H1N5); Dataset-2 (H7N3, H6N2, H1N3); Dataset-3 (H5N2, H3N1, H1N2); Dataset-4 (H5N3, H7N1, H5N2) \\
3		& No			& Isolate	& SRR31013463, SRR31013465, SRR31013467, SRR31013473 \\

\caption{Benchmark datasets. Sets 1 and 2 are simulated with InSilicoSeq (MiSeq
error model, 500{,}000 read pairs of 301\,bp per dataset), four datasets each;
Set 1 carries one genome per dataset and Set 2 three. Every synthetic genome is a
reassortant-like chimera assembled from eight influenza A segments, each drawn
from a different strain, so the listed subtype is derived from the genome's own
HA and NA segments rather than inherited from any single source strain. Per-segment
accessions and donor strains are given in
Tables~\ref{tab:syn-isolate-sources} and~\ref{tab:syn-mixed-sources}.
\label{tab:datasets}}
\end{table}
